notes: Cross-tier interop fixture for the signed-envelope wire protocol. Every Runar SDK (TS/Go/Rust/Python/Zig/Ruby/Java) must consume this and produce byte-identical canonical_json output + verify the valid envelope + reject each tampered envelope with the listed reason.

canonical_json_vectors._notes: Empty key MUST sort before astral plane char in UTF-16 code-unit order (not UTF-8 byte order). Gates Zig D1 fix.

Astral-plane char U+1F600 vs BMP char U+E000. UTF-16 sort: high surrogate 0xD83D < 0xE000 ⇒ astral first. UTF-8 byte sort: 0xF0… > 0xEE… ⇒ BMP first. Triggers a byte-vs-UTF-16 divergence that v18 misses (empty key compares equal under both orders).
Boolean false MUST be preserved verbatim. Gates Ruby D4 fix (the `value[k] || value[k.to_sym]` fallthrough silently rewrote falsy values).

Float at the ECMA-262 1e21 boundary MUST emit `1e+21`. The D5 divergence is fixed: every tier now emits the spec ECMA-262 Number::toString form via its `*Ecma262Double` formatter (Go appendEcma262Double, Rust format_ecma262_double, Python _format_double, Zig appendEcma262Double, Ruby format_ecma262_double, Java formatEcma262Double; TS uses the native JS formatter). `expected` is the spec form and is enforced as a byte-parity gate across all tiers.

Tiny float MUST emit `1e-300` (no trailing `.0`). The D5 divergence is fixed: every tier's `*Ecma262Double` formatter now emits the spec ECMA-262 Number::toString form, so all tiers produce `1e-300` (no trailing `.0`). `expected` is the spec form and is enforced as a byte-parity gate across all tiers.

canonical_json_rejection_vectors._notes: Lone surrogate (U+D800 with no low-surrogate partner) is invalid Unicode per RFC 8785 and MUST be rejected. The D6 fix has landed: every tier now rejects this input — TS (canonical-json.ts: lone-surrogate code path), Go (sdk_envelope.go: WTF-8 0xED,0xA0..0xBF detection), Python (envelope.py: 0xD800..0xDFFF check), Zig (sdk_envelope.zig: error.LoneSurrogate), Ruby (envelope.rb: U+D800..U+DFFF raise), Java (Envelope.java: Character.isHighSurrogate/isLowSurrogate check). Rust cannot represent a lone surrogate in its `&str` type at all (structurally rejected at the type boundary). The Go interop test `packages/runar-go/sdk_envelope_interop_test.go` (TestEnvelopeInterop_CanonicalJSONRejectionVectors) asserts this rejection against this vector. This vector now ENFORCES rejection across all tiers. The input is supplied as a UTF-16 code-unit array so each tier constructs the string deterministically without relying on its JSON parser's lone-surrogate handling.
canonical_json_rejection_vectors.description: object with a value containing the lone high surrogate U+D800

rejection_vectors._notes: The payload is well-formed JSON by the grammar but contains an UNPAIRED SURROGATE escape (\ud800 with no low-surrogate partner), so the string it denotes is not well-formed Unicode. Measured before the fix, on the same envelope: ts / go / python / java accepted it and fell through to 'bad-sig', while rust / ruby / zig rejected it at the parse step with 'bad-json' — four tiers against three, returning different VerifyEnvelopeReason for identical wire input. The project already holds that a lone surrogate is invalid Unicode and must be rejected (vector v22, audit D6); verifyEnvelope hashes the payload RAW, so canonicalJson's detector never sees it and each tier needs the check on the payload text itself.

note_on_pubkey_not_allowed: pubkey-not-allowed cannot be expressed in a tier-agnostic fixture: it depends on caller-supplied expected_keys. Each tier verifies this reason in its own unit tests by passing a non-matching allowlist; the wire bytes are independent.
depth_vectors_notes: R-260. verifyEnvelope parses the payload with each tier's stock JSON library and used to inherit that library's recursion cap, which differs per tier. Measured on ONE envelope (priv=1, live clock, payload {"deep":<N-deep array>,...}): ts/go/python/zig accepted every depth probed (zig to 100001), ruby flipped to bad-json at total depth 101 (JSON.parse default max_nesting: 100), rust at total depth 128 (serde_json RECURSION_LIMIT), and JAVA THREW StackOverflowError OUT OF verify (Json.java readValue/readObject/readArray are mutually recursive with no cap and Envelope.verify catches Exception, not Error) -- at ~5000 deep on a default JVM stack and ~1000 deep under -Xss512k, i.e. the threshold was a JVM launch flag, not a protocol property. Every tier now enforces MAX_ENVELOPE_PAYLOAD_DEPTH = 100 (this file's payload_depth_limit) on the payload TEXT, with a NON-RECURSIVE bracket scan run immediately before the stock parser, so the answer is the same everywhere and the guard itself cannot overflow. depth = the number of containers enclosing a value, 1-based, outermost = 1; 100 accepted, 101 rejected. 100 is Ruby's native JSON.parse default EXACTLY and sits 27 below rust's 127, so no tier has to hand-roll or reconfigure its parser to stay inside it, and it is far above what the wire needs (deepest checked-in conformance artifact: depth 15; this file: 6). It is deliberately the SAME number as canonicalJson's emit-side bound -- if parse were the smaller of the two, a tier could emit a legal, correctly-signed envelope another tier is physically unable to parse. Over-limit rejects as bad-json, the reason two tiers already returned natively and the reason the R-115 lone-surrogate text guard uses.

depth_vectors._notes: Exactly at MAX_ENVELOPE_PAYLOAD_DEPTH (1 outer object + 99 nested arrays = 100). Validly signed by alice (priv=1). This is the control with teeth: an over-strict depth guard, or one that counts off by one, reddens HERE.

One level past the limit (1 outer object + 100 nested arrays = 101). Its signature is VALID for its payload, so a tier that fails to enforce the depth bound returns ok:true rather than a different rejection reason — the assertion cannot pass by accident on a bad-sig fallthrough.

signing_vectors_notes: GAP-064 cross-tier signing reproduction. Each tier, signing the SAME payload with the SAME key (alice priv=1) via RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA whose nonce HMAC uses PLAIN SHA-256, MUST produce the BYTE-IDENTICAL low-S DER signature listed in expected_sig. expected_payload = canonicalJson({...data, nonce, expiresAt}); expected_sig = low-S DER of deterministic ECDSA over sha256(expected_payload) signed directly (the digest is the message representative — do NOT re-hash). Generated via the TS reference (runar-ir-schema canonicalJsonStringify + @bsv/sdk primitives/ECDSA sign with forceLowS=true).

signing_vectors._notes: Non-ASCII BMP key (用户), astral-plane emoji key (🔥 = U+1F525), and a Latin-1 value (héllo). Exercises UTF-16 code-unit key ordering AND UTF-8 payload-byte hashing simultaneously: any tier that diverges on either canonicalization or nonce-hash will produce a different signature.
